title: Bundibugyo Virus Disease in 2026 — Clinical and Public Health Responses
snippet:
The 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease illustrates the progress achieved in pandemic preparedness of medical countermeasures, but challenges remain for responses to filovirus disease outbreaks. Effective outbreak control requires the integration of surveillance, diagnostics, clinical management, infection prevention, community engagement, and medical countermeasures within a coordinated public health framework. Evidence supporting cross-protective vaccines and antibodies suggests that [...] The current outbreak highlights a recurring challenge in emerging infectious diseases: outbreaks often occur before pathogen-specific vaccines and therapeutics are available. Although substantial progress has been made in the development of medical countermeasures against Ebola virus, Sudan virus, and Marburg virus, Bundibugyo virus has received comparatively less attention because of its limited historical effects. As a result, no licensed vaccines or therapeutics specifically targeting [...] •

Currently, no licensed vaccines or approved therapeutics that are specific to Bundibugyo virus are available. However, studies involving nonhuman primates and human serum have shown the potential for cross-protection from vaccines developed for Ebola virus. Data from these studies support a prototype-pathogen approach to vaccine development, with pathogen-specific medical countermeasures advanced rapidly in parallel.
